title: Hospitality businesses are most likely to be struggling to fill vacancies
meta_description: With the number of UK job vacancies at a record high, some industries are reporting difficulties in recruiting new staff. A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage.

breadcrumb.text: Hospitality businesses are most likely to be struggling to fill vacancies

lede: With the number of UK job vacancies at a record high, some industries are reporting difficulties in recruiting new staff. A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage.

body.text: 16 September 2021
Hospitality businesses are more than twice as likely as other industries to be experiencing challenges in filling vacancies compared with normal expectations for this time of year.

Between [23 August and 5 September 2021](https://www.ons.gov.uk/businessindustryandtrade/business/businessservices/bulletins/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy/9september2021), 30% of hospitality businesses said that vacancies were more difficult to fill than normal. This compares with 13% across all industries (up from 9% in early August).

Vacancy challenges are more common for larger businesses. Excluding those with fewer than 10 employees, 41% of businesses across all industries were struggling to fill vacancies in late August, up from 32% earlier in the month.

These difficulties coincide with a very busy time for recruitment, according to the latest [labour market data](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/bulletins/jobsandvacanciesintheuk/september2021), with hospitality among several industries posting record numbers of vacancies in June to August 2021.
Aside from hospitality (30%), the water (27%) and health (23%) industries were most likely to be finding it more difficult than normal to recruit staff in late August.

In the transport and storage sector, 15% of businesses were struggling to fill jobs. This may partly reflect reports of a [shortage of heavy goods vehicle (HGV) drivers](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/57810729). However, despite being mainly employed in transport and storage, HGV drivers only account for around 1 in 10 jobs in the industry as a whole.

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: Businesses across all industries said that a lack of suitable applicants was the main reason for being unable to fill vacancies in late August 2021, with transport and storage firms the most likely to cite a lack of EU applicants specifically.

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: Of all businesses that were experiencing recruitment challenges, one in four (25%) said that a reduced number of EU applicants was a factor. This rises to almost one in two (46%) transport and storage businesses, the highest of any sector.

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: Transport and storage companies were also most likely to report an increased number of vacancies for “other reasons” (47%).

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: The survey question allows multiple responses, so it could be that some businesses are experiencing recruitment challenges because of a lack of EU applicants as well as “other reasons” (which could include border controls, retirements or difficulty in getting an HGV licence at short notice).

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: Some EU workers have left the labour market during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. The [number of EU nationals employed in the UK](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/datasets/employmentbycountryofbirthandnationalityemp06) fell by 8.7% between January to March 2020 and April to June 2021. Meanwhile, the total number of people in employment fell by 2.4% over the same period.

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: Industries experiencing recruitment challenges because of reduced EU applicants have also been affected by a fall in EU workers, according to the Business Insights and Conditions Survey (BICS).

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: In early August, transport and storage and hospitality businesses were the most likely to say they had fewer EU workers than in previous years (7%).

body.h2: A lack of EU applicants is contributing to recruitment challenges, particularly in transport and storage
body.text: Data show that the [number of EU HGV drivers fell by 43% in the year ending March 2021](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/adhocs/13636hgvdriversbyageandnationality) compared with the previous year, while the fall in EU workers in hospitality may partly reflect an overall decline in employment within the industry.

body.h2: The number of job vacancies is rising quickly as coronavirus (COVID-19) restrictions ease
body.text: The number of job vacancies is rising quickly as coronavirus (COVID-19) restrictions ease

body.h2: The number of job vacancies is rising quickly as coronavirus (COVID-19) restrictions ease
body.text: There were 1,034,000 [job vacancies in the UK](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/bulletins/jobsandvacanciesintheuk/september2021) in June to August 2021, an increase of 35.2% (269,300) on the previous quarter and the highest since the series began in 2001.

body.h2: The number of job vacancies is rising quickly as coronavirus (COVID-19) restrictions ease
body.text: The hospitality and transport and storage industries were among those with a record number of vacancies in June to August, with job openings up by 59.1% and 32.5% respectively compared with pre-pandemic (January to March 2020).

body.h2: The number of job vacancies is rising quickly as coronavirus (COVID-19) restrictions ease
body.text: While vacancies are at record levels, the [total number of employees on UK payrolls](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/earningsandworkinghours/bulletins/earningsandemploymentfrompayasyouearnrealtimeinformationuk/september2021) is around the same as it was in February 2020.

body.h2: The number of job vacancies is rising quickly as coronavirus (COVID-19) restrictions ease
body.text: Among industries, payrolled employment was generally rising in August 2021, but remained below pre-pandemic levels by as much as 6.0% in hospitality and 10.2% in arts and recreation.

This reverses the trend seen in the second and third quarters of 2020, when there were more job leavers than starters.

body.h2: London is behind the rest of the UK for job openings
body.text: London is behind the rest of the UK for job openings

body.h2: London is behind the rest of the UK for job openings
body.text: Similar to the overall trend in vacancies, [data from Adzuna](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/economicoutputandproductivity/output/datasets/onlinejobadvertestimates) show that online job adverts are above pre-pandemic levels.

body.h2: London is behind the rest of the UK for job openings
body.text: However, there is wide variation between regions.

body.h2: London is behind the rest of the UK for job openings
body.text: By 10 September 2021, the number of online job adverts in the North East was 72% higher than in February 2020, but only 12% higher in London.

body.h2: London is behind the rest of the UK for job openings
body.text: London has also seen a slower recovery in payrolled employment than other regions. The number of people on payrolls in London remained 1.8% lower in August 2021 than in February 2020, whereas at a national level it is now equal to pre-pandemic numbers.
